# Read-back

One person is running a complete plasmid DNA analysis workflow on a single 5 mL bacterial culture. The work has three sequential phases: first, a plasmid miniprep (spin-column purification) that yields purified plasmid DNA; second, a diagnostic restriction digest using two enzymes (EcoRI and HindIII) to cut the plasmid into fragments; and third, an agarose gel electrophoresis to separate and visualize those fragments alongside a 1 kb DNA ladder. The protocol must finish as soon as the work allows, with no external deadline. The limiting shared resources are one benchtop centrifuge, one microcentrifuge, one 37 °C heat block, one 65 °C heat block, a microwave, one spectrophotometer, and one gel rig. A key scheduling opportunity is that the gel can be cast and set (steps 9–11) while the culture is pelleting and lysing, and the ladder and loading dye can be prepared (step 15) ten minutes into the 60-minute digest incubation, so those steps run in parallel with the main path rather than sequentially. One operator manages all tasks.
